title: When will OpenAI achieve AGI?
claim_or_use: Current market probabilities, volume, contract timeline, settlement wording, and trading restrictions
notes: Snapshot on 2026-08-26 showed 15% before 2027, 36.8% before 2028, 48.1% before 2030, and $910,268 volume; live values change. The 2026 contract resolves on an OpenAI announcement, not an independent AGI benchmark.

title: Working with Event Contracts
claim_or_use: Binary YES/NO contract mechanics, $1/$0 settlement, order matching, spreads, and the probability interpretation of prices
notes: First-party educational material; market microstructure and fee details can change over time.

title: Market Outcomes
claim_or_use: Settlement follows each contract's terms, source, and outcome-determination rules
notes: Useful for distinguishing the real-world concept from the legally settleable event.

title: CFTC Designates KalshiEX LLC as a Contract Market
claim_or_use: Kalshi's status as a CFTC-designated contract market
notes: Designation date in CFTC materials is November 3, 2020; press release published November 4.

title: Prediction Markets
claim_or_use: Evidence that prediction-market forecasts are often accurate and can outperform moderately sophisticated benchmarks; contract-design considerations
notes: Published version appeared in Journal of Economic Perspectives 18(2), 2004.

title: Interpreting Prediction Market Prices as Probabilities
claim_or_use: Conditions under which binary-market prices approximate mean beliefs, and reasons they can be biased
notes: Supports the chapter's caution that a quoted price is useful but not an objective physical probability.

author_or_institution: Joyce E. Berg; Forrest D. Nelson; Thomas A. Rietz
title: Prediction market accuracy in the long run
claim_or_use: Iowa Electronic Markets comparison with 964 presidential polls; market closer to eventual vote split 74% of the time
notes: Study covers U.S. presidential elections from 1988 through 2004; not evidence that every prediction market outperforms every poll.

title: Interpreting the predictions of prediction markets
claim_or_use: Formal caution that equilibrium contract price does not uniquely reveal the distribution or a single objective probability of trader beliefs
notes: Used as counterweight to a simplistic price-equals-probability interpretation.

author_or_institution: Erik Brynjolfsson; Danielle Li; Lindsey R. Raymond
title: Generative AI at Work
claim_or_use: Field evidence from 5,172 customer-support agents; AI assistance raised issues resolved per hour by about 15% on average, with larger gains for less experienced workers
notes: Quarterly Journal of Economics 140(2), 2025. Effects were heterogeneous; strongest workers saw much smaller gains and some quality declines.

title: Large Firms With At Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
claim_or_use: Recent U.S. business AI adoption rates by firm size and sector; national use around 17%-20%, with 37% of firms with 250+ employees reporting use
notes: BTOS wording changed in November 2025 to ask about AI use in any business function; comparisons with earlier survey wording require caution.

author_or_institution: Kathryn Bonney; Cory Breaux; Emin Dinlersoz; Lucia Foster; John Haltiwanger; Aditya Pande
title: The Microstructure of AI Diffusion: Evidence from Firms, Business Functions, and Worker Tasks
claim_or_use: Nationally representative evidence that 18% of firms used AI during Nov. 2025-Jan. 2026, 32% employment-weighted, with adoption concentrated in large and knowledge-intensive firms and often limited to a few functions
notes: Working paper CES-26-25; among adopting firms 57% used AI in three or fewer business functions.

author_or_institution: Erik Brynjolfsson; Avinash Collis; Felix Eggers; Sophia Kazinnik; David Nguyen
title: What is Generative AI Worth?
claim_or_use: Choice-experiment estimates of U.S. generative-AI consumer surplus, including roughly 115 million adult users and about $172 billion annual aggregate surplus by March 2026
notes: Willingness-to-accept estimates are welfare measures, not observed revenue; mean and median user valuations differ substantially.

title: Schumpeterian Profits in the American Economy: Theory and Measurement
claim_or_use: Historical evidence and framework showing that innovators may capture only a small share of the social surplus created by technological change
notes: Nordhaus estimates producers captured about 2.2% of total innovation surplus over 1948-2001; this is historical context, not a parameter to apply mechanically to AI.

title: Technical Performance — 2026 AI Index Report
claim_or_use: Evidence that frontier model capabilities continued advancing rapidly and that several benchmarks were saturating, while benchmark performance should not be equated with general intelligence
notes: Secondary synthesis of underlying benchmarks and studies; used only for broad capability context.

title: Economy — 2026 AI Index Report
claim_or_use: Context on rapid AI investment and adoption alongside task-dependent productivity evidence and still-mixed macroeconomic effects
notes: Used as a synthesis and counterweight; chapter relies on primary Census and academic studies for central quantitative claims.

title: Railroad investment and receiverships, 1892-1897
claim_or_use: U.S. railway mileage growth and scale of 1890s railroad receiverships: 2,510 railways and 60,012 miles entered receivership from 1892-1897
notes: Retrospective 1918 statement using historical railway figures; reports mileage of 52,922 in 1870 and 192,940 in 1900 and nearly one-third of national mileage entering receivership during 1892-1897.

title: Railroads, Reallocation, and the Rise of American Manufacturing
claim_or_use: Evidence that expanded railroad market access substantially increased manufacturing productivity and economic activity
notes: Used to establish that railroad infrastructure created real productivity gains rather than being merely speculative construction.

title: Collusive Investments in Technological Compatibility: Lessons from U.S. Railroads in the Late 19th Century
claim_or_use: 1886 conversion of roughly 13,000 miles of southern railroad track to standard gauge and resulting shift of freight traffic toward rail
notes: Published in Management Science in 2020; supports the role of network compatibility in raising the usefulness of existing infrastructure.

title: Spatial Competition, Strategic Entry Responses, and the North Dakota Railroad War of 1905
claim_or_use: Case evidence that individually strategic railroad entry and incumbent response could generate overexpansion and potentially unprofitable capacity
notes: Used as counterpoint to a pure-mania explanation: overcapacity can emerge from strategic competition under uncertainty.

title: Does Innovation Cause Stock Market Runups? Evidence from the Great Crash
claim_or_use: Evidence that investors placed increasing value on corporate knowledge capital in the 1920s and that innovation contributed to the late-1920s market runup
notes: American Economic Review 98(4); used to show that technology-stock enthusiasm can respond to genuine innovation rather than pure fantasy.

title: Stock Market Crash of 1929
claim_or_use: Dates and scale of October 1929 market declines and broader market context
notes: Used only for broad crash chronology; chapter does not attribute the Great Crash to radio.

title: The Telecommunications Boom and Bust
claim_or_use: Reconstruction of late-1990s telecom investment boom, sector valuation collapse, long-haul fiber overcapacity, and falling capacity prices
notes: Contemporaneous retrospective; distinguishes demand expectations, financing conditions, and physical overcapacity.

title: Bandwidth Glut Lives On
claim_or_use: TeleGeography evidence that long-haul bandwidth prices continued falling despite rapidly rising internet traffic; U.S. route prices down 55% in a year and over 90% over four years
notes: Secondary source reporting TeleGeography data; also reports only about 11% of major-city fiber lit at the time. Used for the coexistence of traffic growth and price collapse.

author_or_institution: WorldCom Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
title: WorldCom Form 10-K for fiscal year 2002
claim_or_use: WorldCom's July 2002 Chapter 11 filing and acknowledgement that prior financial statements required restatement for GAAP failures
notes: Used to avoid treating WorldCom as a clean example of overcapacity alone; accounting fraud was material to its collapse.

author_or_institution: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
title: Review of Maritime Transport 2008
claim_or_use: Record 2008 merchant-vessel order book: 10,053 ships and 495 million dwt, equal to 44% of the existing fleet by tonnage; dry-bulk orders of 222 million dwt
notes: Provides the pre-crisis order-book and fleet context; the report also noted cancellations emerging by mid-2008.

author_or_institution: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
title: Review of Maritime Transport 2009
claim_or_use: Baltic Dry Index fell more than 90% from its May 2008 peak by year-end while fleet capacity continued expanding; dry-bulk fleet of about 418 million dwt faced a 292 million dwt order book by March 2009
notes: Used to show demand deterioration colliding with capacity ordered during the prior boom; order book was roughly 70% of the existing dry-bulk fleet.

title: Waves in Ship Prices and Investment
claim_or_use: Dry-bulk evidence that high ship earnings and prices induce fleet investment but forecast low future returns because competitive capacity responses make earnings mean revert
notes: Published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics in 2015; authors' model also finds firms over-extrapolate demand shocks and partly neglect competitors' investment response.

title: Real and Financial Industry Booms and Busts
claim_or_use: Evidence that in competitive industries high valuations, investment, and financing are followed by lower operating cash flow and abnormal stock returns, with much weaker patterns in concentrated industries
notes: Used as cross-industry support and counterevidence that competitive structure matters; the result is not a universal law of high investment.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026
claim_or_use: Current AI scarcity signal used in chapter handoff: FY2026 revenue of $215.9B up 65%, GAAP gross margin of 71.1%, and full-year Data Center revenue up 68%
notes: Primary company disclosure. Strong margins and growth are presented as evidence of current scarcity economics, not proof that future supply will create a glut.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2027
claim_or_use: Current accelerator-demand signal: quarterly revenue $96.2B, Data Center revenue $89.0B up 117% year over year, 75% GAAP gross margin, and $108B next-quarter revenue outlook
notes: Primary disclosure published one day before drafting. Outlook excludes Data Center compute revenue from China; current margins and demand are not assumed to persist indefinitely.

title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call
claim_or_use: AI revenue run rate above $37B, Q3 capex of $31.9B, roughly two thirds of capex in short-lived GPUs/CPUs, Q4 capex expected above $40B, calendar-2026 capex expectation roughly $190B, and capacity constraints through 2026
notes: Management guidance is forward-looking. Microsoft said about $25B of calendar-2026 capex reflected higher component pricing and characterized long-lived assets separately from short-lived compute equipment.

title: Amazon.com Announces Second Quarter Results
claim_or_use: AWS Q2 revenue of $42.2B up 37%, AWS operating income $16.6B, AI and chips businesses each above $25B annual revenue run rates, and trailing free cash flow of negative $7.6B driven mainly by increased AI property/equipment purchases
notes: Primary company release. Free-cash-flow decline reflects heavy investment and does not by itself establish poor future returns.

title: Meta Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results
claim_or_use: Initial 2026 capex guidance of $115B-$135B and management expectation that infrastructure would drive most expense growth while operating income could still exceed 2025
notes: Forward-looking guidance; used to establish the starting point for Meta's 2026 infrastructure plan.

title: Meta Reports First Quarter 2026 Results
claim_or_use: Raised 2026 capex guidance to $125B-$145B, citing higher component pricing and additional data-center costs for future-year capacity
notes: Forward-looking guidance; demonstrates the spending plan increased as capacity and component costs changed.

title: Meta Announces New Strategic Venture with BlackRock to Develop Data Center in El Paso
claim_or_use: One-gigawatt El Paso campus under construction with approximately $14B total development cost for buildings and long-lived power, cooling, and connectivity infrastructure; structure uses outside infrastructure capital
notes: Campus expected to begin bringing capacity online in 2028; project illustrates committed long-lived infrastructure, not current installed compute capacity.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026
claim_or_use: Rubin platform claim of up to 10x lower inference token cost versus Blackwell and evidence of rapid hardware-generation efficiency improvement
notes: Vendor performance claim; used to illustrate the direction and potential magnitude of effective-capacity improvement, not as an independently validated realized fleet-wide cost reduction.

title: API Platform
claim_or_use: Current frontier-model API prices used to show that the unit price of inference varies widely by model and is actively competed downward as capability changes
notes: Live pricing page; prices change over time and model generations are not directly capability-equivalent, so the chapter avoids a simplistic historical price index.

title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update
claim_or_use: Reference-case U.S. data-center electricity use of 649 TWh in 2030, 11.8% of national electricity, with a 9.5%-15.3% scenario range
notes: Forecast based on planned IT-equipment shipments, per-device energy use, cooling simulations, facility types, and locations; scenario output is not committed load.

title: Energy and AI — Energy demand from AI
claim_or_use: Global data-center electricity demand estimate of about 415 TWh in 2024 and base-case projection of about 945 TWh by 2030; accelerated servers drive nearly half of the increase; cooling shares vary widely by facility type
notes: Forecast includes alternative Lift-Off, High Efficiency, and Headwinds cases; chapter treats the base case as a scenario rather than a certainty.

title: Queued Up: 2026 Edition, Characteristics of Power Plants Seeking Transmission Interconnection As of the End of 2025
claim_or_use: More than 2,060 GW of generation and storage actively seeking U.S. transmission interconnection at end-2025; active queue volume fell about 10% year over year and most proposed projects historically withdraw
notes: Dataset covers operators representing about 98% of installed U.S. generating capacity; queues are indicators of development interest, not forecasts of completed plants.

title: FERC Launches Aggressive Targeted Action to Speed Large Load Integration
claim_or_use: FERC ordered six regional grid operators to justify or reform tariffs governing data centers and other large loads, demonstrating that load-interconnection rules are an active bottleneck
notes: Regulatory response may accelerate connections; used as evidence both of current constraint and institutional adaptation.

title: Commissioner Rosner's Remarks on the Large Load Show Cause Orders, E-7 to E-12
claim_or_use: Cost Recovery Agreements intended to protect other customers if grid infrastructure is built for a large load that does not materialize
notes: Used to illustrate the financial problem of planning infrastructure before uncertain large-load projects are energized.

author_or_institution: U.S. Department of Energy Office of Electricity
title: Supply Chain and Market Analysis
claim_or_use: Distribution-transformer lead times increased from roughly 3-6 months in 2019 to 12-30 months in 2023; DOE is pursuing interoperability and specification standardization to shorten production times
notes: 2023 is the latest comparable lead-time data cited by DOE; constraint predates the current AI buildout and has multiple causes.

author_or_institution: Nuoa Lei; Jun Lu; Arman Shehabi; Eric R. Masanet
title: The water use of data center workloads: A review and assessment of key determinants
claim_or_use: Data-center workload water use varies by more than 10,000-fold across conditions; key determinants include server efficiency, grid water intensity, utilization, cooling system, infrastructure efficiency, climate, and refresh cycle
notes: Supports a site- and workload-specific treatment of water impacts rather than a single universal water-per-query figure.

title: Meta Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Results
claim_or_use: January 2025 reassessment increased estimated useful life of certain servers and network assets to 5.5 years and was expected to reduce 2025 depreciation expense by about $2.9B on assets already in service
notes: Accounting-estimate change is used to explain timing of expense recognition, not as evidence of impropriety.

title: Investor FAQs and General Information — Depreciation
claim_or_use: Alphabet depreciates servers and network equipment generally over six years and regularly evaluates useful lives for technological obsolescence, planned use, and utilization
notes: Current IR glossary; data-center and office buildings have materially longer lives, illustrating different clocks within technical infrastructure.

title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call
claim_or_use: Investor challenge to six-year server capitalization versus 2.5-year average commercial RPO; management said many GPUs were already contracted for most or all of their useful lives and software improves aging-fleet efficiency
notes: Strong counterevidence to assuming a six-year accounting life necessarily implies utilization risk; contract coverage is management disclosure rather than independently observed fleet utilization.

title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call
claim_or_use: Q3 capex of $31.9B; roughly two thirds in short-lived GPUs/CPUs and remaining spend in long-lived assets intended to monetize for 15+ years; Microsoft Cloud gross margin 66% while AI investment pressured margins
notes: Shows that one capex total contains assets with very different economic lives and uses; company also reported capacity constraints.

title: Microsoft Fiscal Year 2026 Fourth Quarter Earnings Release
claim_or_use: FY2026 additions to property and equipment of $115.948B versus $64.551B in FY2025; depreciation, amortization, and other cash-flow adjustment of $38.534B versus $29.433B
notes: PP&E includes more than AI infrastructure and the cash-flow adjustment includes more than depreciation; chapter uses the figures only to illustrate the scale and lag of capital entering the expense base.

title: FY26 Q4 Investor Metrics
claim_or_use: Microsoft Cloud FY2026 revenue $214.4B with 66% gross margin, showing strong current cloud economics despite heavy infrastructure investment
notes: Microsoft Cloud is broader than Azure or generative AI; used as counterevidence against treating current hyperscaler infrastructure as unmonetized.

title: Amazon.com Announces Second Quarter Results
claim_or_use: AWS Q2 revenue $42.232B and operating income $16.621B alongside trailing twelve-month free-cash-flow outflow of $7.6B driven primarily by a $66.1B year-over-year increase in property-and-equipment purchases
notes: AWS operating economics and consolidated free cash flow are different measures; the chapter uses their coexistence to show why current profit does not settle the return on incremental capex.

title: Meta Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
claim_or_use: Q2 depreciation and amortization rose to $6.356B from $4.342B a year earlier; operating margin was 31% versus 43% as total costs and expenses rose 55%
notes: Many expense categories affected the margin change; chapter does not attribute the decline to depreciation alone.

title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT-5.6
claim_or_use: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna API prices by 80% and Terra by 20% after serving-efficiency improvements, illustrating simultaneous falling unit prices and attempts to expand economical demand
notes: Vendor claims about efficiency and customer economics are not independent market-wide measurements; observed list-price changes are used directly.

title: 2025 Q4 Earnings Call
claim_or_use: Alphabet depreciation rose from $15.3B in 2024 to $21.1B in 2025; roughly 60% of 2025 technical-infrastructure investment went to servers and 40% to data centers/networking, with similar mix expected in 2026
notes: Management expected depreciation growth to accelerate in 2026; asset mix figures are company disclosure and do not isolate generative-AI returns.
